reason: S1 adds three public safe APIs whose status-code and output-pointer protocols are not exercised directly by H0. Although H0 reaches much of their internal behavior indirectly through xmlParseURI, xmlBuildURI, and xmlBuildRelativeURI, those wrappers discard the safe APIs' integer results and always supply ordinary output pointers, leaving distinct public-call semantics unreachable.
evidence: include/libxml/uri.h newly declares xmlParseURISafe, xmlBuildURISafe, and xmlBuildRelativeURISafe as public entry points.
fuzz/uri.c calls xmlParseURI, xmlBuildURI, and xmlBuildRelativeURI but never calls any of the new *Safe functions.
xmlParseURISafe returns distinct success, invalid-input, and allocation-failure codes and permits uriOut == NULL; xmlParseURI always calls it as xmlParseURISafe(str, &uri) and discards the status.
xmlBuildURISafe exposes an int result plus xmlChar **valPtr, while xmlBuildURI always supplies &out and discards the status.
xmlBuildRelativeURISafe explicitly handles valPtr == NULL by returning 1 and initializes *valPtr = NULL; xmlBuildRelativeURI cannot exercise that protocol because it always supplies &val.
The missing public entry points and output/status combinations exist only in S1, so the material gap is commit-induced rather than historical.
recommended_action: Extend the URI harness to call all three *Safe APIs directly, vary optional/null output pointers where permitted, inspect the returned status classes, free successful outputs, and retain allocation-failure injection around these calls.
